top_strength: When Patty pushed back with a cheaper competitor quote, Daniel stayed calm and specific rather than defensive — he clearly broke down what the lower price was actually missing (per-pound damage liability vs. the $2,000 No Worries coverage, no hidden add-on fees, trip-fee logic), which is exactly how the differentiators should be used to win a price objection.
coaching_note: Patty explicitly said she wanted to keep the move 'under five hours' because it 'gets expensive' — that was the moment to run a real Save Your Ass prep speech (consolidate loose items, take a carload) to give her concrete ways to actually lower the bill, instead of only defending the price after the fact; building that speech into every cost-sensitive call is the highest-leverage fix here.
phone_presence_notes: Daniel is patient and polite throughout, especially in handling the price objection, but the rambling, filler-heavy delivery keeps the call feeling transactional rather than warm and confident.
audio_review_reason: Transcript is heavily garbled with fragmented, run-on phrasing throughout (especially in the pricing/estimate section, e.g. the confused restart around the $1,097 figure), making it hard to confirm actual vocal tone and pacing from text alone.
